pageScale="1" pageWidth="850" pageHeight="1100" math="0" shadow="0"> <root> <mxCell id="0" /> <mxCell id="1" parent="0" /> <UserObject label="" tooltip="<pre>
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

def sample_dot_products(M, max_dim, scaling = False):
 dims = np.arange(1, max_dim + 1)
 avg_abs_dot_products = []
 
 for d in dims:
 X = np.random.multivariate_normal(mean=np.zeros(d), cov=np.identity(d), size = M)
 Y = np.random.multivariate_normal(mean=np.zeros(d), cov=np.identity(d), size = M)

 if scaling:
 factor = 1 / np.sqrt(d)
 else:
 factor = 1

 dots = (X @ Y.T) * factor
 
 avg_abs_dot_products.append(np.mean(np.abs(dots)))
 
 return dims, avg_abs_dot_products

M = 1000 # Number of dot products sampled per dimension
max_dim = 100 # Maximum dimension

dims, avg_abs_dot_products = sample_dot_products(M, max_dim)
dims, scaled_avg_abs_dot_products = sample_dot_products(M, max_dim, scaling=True)


fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 5))

ax[0].scatter(dims, avg_abs_dot_products, marker='.', linestyle='-')
ax[0].set_xlabel("Dimension")
ax[0].set_ylabel("Mean Dot Product Magnitude")
ax[0].set_title("Unscaled Dot Product Magnitude vs. Dimension")
ax[0].grid()

ax[1].scatter(dims, scaled_avg_abs_dot_products, marker='.', linestyle='-')
ax[1].set_xlabel("Dimension")
ax[1].set_ylabel("Mean Dot Product Magnitude")
ax[1].set_title("Square Root Scaled Dot Product Magnitude vs. Dimension")
ax[1].grid()

plt.tight_layout()

width="55" height="55" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="X5mycXT-UQ77Il74ekUl-96" value="<div>Given a sequence of \(T_d\) tokens, the decoder has access to tokens 1 through \(T_d\) during its forward pass. Consider one of these tokens, token \(j\), where \(1 \leq j \leq T_d\).</div><div><br></div><div>During one forward pass in training, the decoder takes a look at each token \(j\) and makes a guess for the \(j+1\)-th token. This is done for all \(j\) in a single forward pass. Since the \(j+1\)-th token is present in the sequence already, we need to hide it from the decoder and make the decoder guess using only the information up to and including the \(j\)-th token.</div><div><br></div>So, \(j\)-th token should "see" only itself and the tokens that preceded it. So, the query for the \(j\)-th token should only attend to the key for the \(j\)-th token and the keys of tokens preceding the \(j\)-th token. The MatMul operation takes all possible inner products between the query vectors and key vectors, so we apply a mask that sets the appropriate elements in the result to \(-\infty\)" id="xDF0bNnMEgLOrBHkTTWm-1" value="<ul><li>There are \(V\) tokens in the model's vocabulary&nbsp;</li><li>\(p_i\) is a length \(V\) vector defining a probability distribution over the vocabulary</li><li>\(p_i[j]\) is the probability that the \(i+1\)-th token in the sequence is equal to token with ID = \(j\).</li><li>Note that the true \(i+1\)-th token in the decoded sequence is not seen by the decoder because we mask it out in Masked Multi-Head Attention.</li><li>During training, we care about all the probability distributions \(p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_{T_d}\) because we know what the next token is. So, we can compute a cross-entropy loss for each \(p_i\) and take an average to get the loss for the batch.</li><li>During inference, we only care about generating the next token, i.e. the \(T_d + 1\)-th token. So we only need to find \(p_{T_d}\) and sample the next token from it.</li></ul>" style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;whiteSpace=wrap;rounded=0;" parent="1" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry x="-1640" y="410" width="732.5" height="180" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="tJaYcOaPAmUDns3Gi-4B-6" value="" style="group" parent="1" vertex="1" connectable="0"> <mxGeometry x="-1342" y="227.5" width="102" height="120" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="tJaYcOaPAmUDns3Gi-4B-4" style="edgeStyle=orthogonalEdgeStyle;rounded=0;orthogonalLoop=1;jettySize=auto;html=1;exitX=0.5;exitY=0;exitDx=0;exitDy=0;" parent="tJaYcOaPAmUDns3Gi-4B-6" source="tJaYcOaPAmUDns3Gi-4B-1" edge="1"> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry"> <mxPoint x="102" y="60.5" as="targetPoint" /> </mxGeometry> </mxCell> <object label="<font style="font-size: 16px;">Softmax</font>" tooltip="<pre>

 out : tensor of shape (B, T_d, V)
</pre>" id="tJaYcOaPAmUDns3Gi-4B-1"> <mxCell style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#000000;strokeWidth=2;rotation=90;" parent="tJaYcOaPAmUDns3Gi-4B-6" vertex="1">
